sources.entry: WallpaperMachine - Native live wallpaper app that plays Wallpaper Engine scene, video and web wallpapers, with Steam Workshop browsing built in.

summary.one_liner: A free, open-source native macOS app that plays Wallpaper Engine scene, video and web wallpapers on the desktop, with Steam Workshop browsing and downloads built in.
summary.what_it_does: The app plays Wallpaper Engine scene, video and web wallpapers as the macOS desktop background, sourced from the Steam Workshop or local files. It has a tabbed window for a library, Workshop and pixiv browsing, and Settings, with a menu bar item for pause, mute and next/previous/random controls. Features include per-display wallpapers, playlists, a battery mode, a playback rule set (such as pausing for covered displays or low battery), and an optional animated lock screen and screen saver (both experimental). Scene rendering uses a Rust core, a C++ scene engine and Metal. The README says scene wallpapers need shared resources from a Wallpaper Engine installation you own, and Workshop downloads need a Steam account that owns Wallpaper Engine.
use_cases: Put animated Wallpaper Engine wallpapers on a Mac desktop
Browse and download Steam Workshop wallpapers
Rotate wallpapers per display with playlists or schedules
Use local videos or pictures as animated desktop backgrounds
Save energy with battery-saving playback rules
Set an animated wallpaper as lock screen or screen saver
how_to_run: Download the free disk image for the latest version from the project's releases page.
Open the disk image and drag WallpaperMachine to Applications.
Open the app; click Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security on first launch (the build is not notarized).
To build from source: python3 scripts/build.py --configuration Release
Package and install with: python3 scripts/package.py --configuration Release --install
notable: Native macOS app for Wallpaper Engine content, not a Windows port, with Steam Workshop browsing and downloads in the app
Per-display wallpapers, mirroring, blurred-backdrop fit and per-display playlists
Battery, Low Power Mode and hot-Mac rules that lower quality or pause playback
Build provenance attestations and SHA-256 checksums for releases; updater refuses unverified disk images
Scene engine and renderer are open source under GPL-3.0-only, with no paid feature tier
caveats: Requires Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 15 Sequoia or later; Intel Macs are not supported
Animated lock screen needs macOS 26 Tahoe or later; screen saver support is experimental on macOS 26+
Workshop downloads and scene wallpapers need a Steam account and Wallpaper Engine ownership; compatibility varies by wallpaper and Application wallpapers do not run
The signed build is not notarized, so macOS requires a manual approval on first launch
keywords: play video on my mac desktop
